rounds.text: T & I Global Ltd trades at an attractive valuation relative to its peers and its own asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.90x on a book value of ₹ 209 against a sector benchmark of 2.31x [E2, E7]. The company is exceptionally well-capitalized with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and zero borrowings, positioning it as almost debt free [E37, E38, E48]. Recent financial performance displays a powerful operational inflection point, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 29% and a compounded profit growth of 214%, alongside quarterly operating margins expanding to 12% in September 2026 [E17, E21, E31]. Cash generation is robust, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs 19 Cr, free cash flow of Rs 18 Cr, and a strong cash conversion of 2.71x for March 2026, which fully backs reported profits [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency has dramatically improved, with requirements dropping from 57.7 days to 14.1 days [E51]. Conceded: historical longer-term sales growth has been subdued at 4% over five years, median return on equity over the last year sits at a modest 7%, and the company currently pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E15, E29].

Conceded: [E35], [E36], [E37]. Despite clean leverage metrics, the valuation is unsupported because a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 174 per share against a higher market price of Rs 189, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -8.9% [E42], [E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price already prices in 1.1% earnings growth, outpacing the base case assumption of 0.0% [E44]. Long-term top-line growth is deeply sluggish, evidenced by compounded sales growth of just 2% over 10 years, 4% over 5 years, and a contraction of -6% over 3 years [E14], [E15], [E16]. Return metrics consistently lag behind sector benchmarks, with the company's ROE of 7.59%, ROCE of 9.71%, and ROA of 4.9% all falling short of their respective sector averages [E8], [E9], [E10]. Operational quality is further undermined by a low 3-year median ROE of 7% and an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E28], [E32]. Finally, shareholder returns are compromised by a 0.00% dividend yield alongside earnings that are padded by Rs 5.51 Cr in other income [E4], [E52], [E55].

Conceded: [E42], [E43]. The bear's fixation on static DCF models ignores the company's accelerating fundamental inflection, evidenced by a massive 214% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months and a stellar 100/100 results score [E21], [E62]. Dismissing the top-line ignores the recent explosive top-line turnaround, with TTM compounded sales growth surging to 29% and quarterly sales leaping 61% year-over-year [E17], [E57]. The asset base trades at a deep discount, with the stock priced at just 0.90x book value and an EV/EBITDA of 7.17x that significantly undercuts the sector benchmark of 12.22x [E2], [E7], [E11]. Furthermore, concerns over cash generation are entirely unfounded given the exceptional 2.71x cash conversion backed by Rs 19 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 18 Cr in free cash flow, all bolstered by a completely debt-free balance sheet [E34], [E35], [E36], [E37]. Operational efficiency is also visibly improving, highlighted by a sharp reduction in working capital requirements from 57.7 days to 14.1 days and a recent two-percentage-point expansion in quarterly operating margins [E31], [E51].

Conceded: [E31], [E51]. The bull’s heavy reliance on recent explosive growth metrics masks a dismal long-term structural reality, characterized by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 2% and a 5-year growth rate of 4% [E14], [E15]. Furthermore, the dramatic trailing twelve-month profit growth of 214% is heavily flattered and rendered low-quality by the inclusion of Rs. 5.51 Cr in other income [E21], [E55]. The underlying operational profitability remains weak and inconsistent, evidenced by a 3-year median return on equity of 7% and a multi-year operating margin compression that dropped two percentage points over three years [E28], [E30], [E32]. Valuation is actually stretched relative to asset reality rather than cheap, since a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 174 against a market price of Rs 189, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -8.9% [E42], [E43]. Finally, despite consistent profit reporting, the firm refuses to distribute any earnings to shareholders, maintaining a stagnant 0.00% dividend yield [E4], [E52].
